title: What causes terrace leaks in Guwahati?
excerpt: Monsoon, flat roofs, and failed membranes — why terrace leaks are so common in Northeast India.
body: Guwahati receives over 1,600mm rainfall annually, mostly concentrated in monsoon months. Flat terrace design — standard in apartment construction — allows water to pond if slope is inadequate. Over time, UV and heat cycling degrade waterproofing membranes. Penetrations around pipes and parapet upturns fail first. The fix starts with diagnosis: flood test and tracing water path before any new coating.

title: Column crack vs settlement crack — how to tell
excerpt: Not all cracks are equal. Learn which patterns need urgent structural attention.
body: Settlement cracks often appear as stair-steps in masonry or diagonal cracks at window corners. Column cracks run through the concrete member itself — often vertical or at beam-column joints. Width matters: cracks over 3mm in structural members warrant professional assessment. In Seismic Zone V, any column crack should be inspected before the next tremor season.

title: PU injection vs epoxy injection — when to use which
excerpt: Both fill cracks — but they work differently. Choosing wrong wastes money.
body: PU (polyurethane) injection reacts with water to expand — ideal for active leaking cracks in basements and terraces. Epoxy injection bonds concrete structurally — used for dry structural cracks in columns and beams where strength restoration is needed. Many projects need both: PU to stop water, epoxy to restore capacity.

title: Carbon fibre wrapping explained for homeowners
excerpt: CFRP adds strength without bulky columns — how it works on Guwahati flats.
body: Carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) sheets are epoxy-bonded to concrete surfaces. They add tensile capacity to weakened columns and beams with minimal thickness — important in occupied flats where space matters. It is not a paint product; surface prep and structural design are critical.

title: Why get NDT before buying a resale flat in Guwahati
excerpt: Hidden defects cost lakhs after purchase. A building strength test is cheap insurance.
body: Rebound hammer, UPV, and cover meter tests reveal honeycomb, low strength concrete, and corroding steel — invisible during a normal flat viewing. In Beltola and Chandmari resale markets, 15–30 year buildings often have monsoon damage. NDT report gives negotiation leverage or avoids a bad purchase.

title: Rising damp vs lateral seepage
excerpt: Both cause damp walls — but fixing the wrong one fails next monsoon.
body: Rising damp shows up to 1m from floor — salt deposits, tide marks. Lateral seepage from adjacent bathroom or external wall affects mid-height patches. Ground floor flats in old Guwahati buildings often have both. Moisture meter profiling at multiple heights distinguishes them.

title: Expansion joints in apartment buildings — why they leak
excerpt: Movement joints are necessary — but failed seals flood parking levels.
body: Multi-block complexes need joints to absorb thermal and seismic movement. Sealant loses elasticity after 5–7 years. Rigid fillers crack. Proper repair uses correct joint width, backing rod, and movement-capable sealant — not cheap silicone.

title: Seismic Zone V — what Guwahati homeowners should know
excerpt: Highest earthquake zone in India. What it means for your building.
body: Guwahati sits in IS seismic Zone V. Older buildings may not meet current ductile detailing standards. Retrofitting — column jacketing, CFRP, joint confinement — reduces collapse risk. It is not optional luxury; it is risk management for your family.

title: Basement waterproofing methods compared
excerpt: Internal tanking, external membrane, injection — which suits Guwahati soil?
body: High water table areas need external cutoff where accessible. Internal crystalline systems work when excavation is impossible. PU injection handles active leaks through cracks. Often a combination is required — diagnosis determines sequence.

title: Concrete spalling — catch it before chunks fall
excerpt: Rust stains and hollow sounds are warnings. Act before balcony edges fail.
body: Spalling starts when steel corrodes inside concrete. Early signs: rust staining, fine cracks parallel to rebar, hollow sound when tapped. Patch repair without steel treatment fails in one monsoon. Proper repair: expose, clean, treat, reinstate with structural mortar.

title: Heat reflective roof coating — does it work in Assam?
excerpt: Weather Cool and similar coatings — real temperature drop or marketing?
body: Reflective coatings reduce surface temperature by up to 14°C on exposed terraces. They also extend underlying waterproofing life by reducing thermal stress. Best applied on stable substrate after leak repair — not over active leaks.

title: Structural audit vs home inspection
excerpt: Property inspectors miss structural issues. Know the difference.
body: Home inspection checks plumbing, electrical, and cosmetics. Structural audit uses NDT, crack mapping, and load review. For resale flats and old commercial buildings in Guwahati, structural audit is the relevant standard.

title: Monsoon building maintenance checklist
excerpt: Pre-monsoon steps every Guwahati building owner should take.
body: Clear terrace drains. Inspect parapet and pipe penetrations. Check expansion joints. Look for new cracks in columns. Test overhead tank overflows. Book professional inspection if building is 15+ years or shows any structural crack.

title: RWA guide: terrace waterproofing decisions
excerpt: How housing societies should evaluate contractor quotes fairly.
body: Compare methodology not just price. Ask: membrane type, slope correction, penetration detail, warranty, and flood test protocol. Cheapest quote often skips parapet upturn and joint treatment — leak returns in one season.

title: Illegal terrace rooms — structural risk
excerpt: Extra load on terrace slab can exceed design capacity.
body: Many Guwahati buildings have unauthorized terrace rooms. Slab may not be designed for additional dead load. Combined with waterproofing failure, risk is significant. Structural check before any terrace use modification.

title: Epoxy flooring for industrial warehouses
excerpt: When concrete dust and forklift traffic need industrial grade floors.
body: Epoxy and polyurethane floor systems handle abrasion, chemical spill, and heavy point loads. Surface prep — grinding and moisture test — determines adhesion. Paltan Bazar and outskirts warehouses benefit from phased bay application.

title: Borewell recharge and rainwater harvesting in Guwahati
excerpt: Heavy rain, falling groundwater — capture and recharge responsibly.
body: Rooftop rainwater can flush toilets and recharge borewells via soak pits — if soil and contamination risks are assessed. Reduces water bill and helps maintain groundwater in urban Guwahati.

title: Building leak FAQ — quick answers for Guwahati
excerpt: Common questions about leaks, cracks, and repair costs.
body: Q: Who fixes basement leaks in Guwahati? A: Building rehabilitation specialists with waterproofing and injection capability — not general painters. Q: Cost? A: Depends on diagnosis — inspection first. Q: How long? A: Terrace systems 7–14 days; column retrofit varies.

title: Micro concreting for honeycomb repair
excerpt: Hollow columns sound bad — micro concreting fills voids without demolition.
body: Honeycomb in columns leaves steel unprotected. High-strength grout injection fills voids. Used with NDT confirmation. Common in buildings with rushed pours during original construction boom.

title: When to call a building doctor vs a contractor
excerpt: Symptoms vs root cause — who should you call first?
body: Call a contractor when you know the fix: new tiles, paint job. Call a building rehabilitation specialist when you have symptoms — leak, crack, damp — but unknown cause. Diagnosis-first approach saves money long term.
